rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Servers, network equipment, and software': 215,874m − 132,836m = 83,038m, against 115,948m of cash additions to PP&E. This counts all server, network and software growth, not only AI, and includes finance-leased assets placed in service. It excludes buildings and land. Forward signals not in the amount: finance lease liabilities of 66,594m (46,172m a year earlier), purchase commitments of 194,060m, leases not yet commenced of $329.1bn 'primarily for datacenters', and commercial RPO of $678bn.

Growth in gross 'Computer equipment and software': 132,836m − 93,780m = 39,056m, against 64,551m of capex. This is the same category later renamed 'Servers, network equipment, and software', with the same FY2025 balance under both names. It counts all server growth, not only AI.
Growth in gross 'Computer equipment and software' (the server category before its rename): 93,780m − 74,961m = 18,819m, against 44,477m of capex. This counts all server growth, not only AI.

Growth in gross 'Computer equipment and software': 74,961m − 60,631m = 14,330m, against 28,107m of capex. This counts all server growth. The year is largely before the AI buildout, so most of it is general cloud.
Growth in gross 'Computer equipment and software': 60,631m − 51,250m = 9,381m, against 23,886m of capex. This counts all server growth in a year before the AI buildout, so it is mostly general cloud.

FY2026 MD&A: 'We will continue to invest in capital expenditures to support growth in our cloud offerings and our investments in AI training and other infrastructure.' This covers total capex, with no amount and no AI share.

The FY2026 MD&A attributes increases to AI in words only. Cost of revenue rose 17.7bn (44%) 'driven by investments in AI infrastructure to support growing customer demand'. R&D rose 3.1bn, driven by compute capacity and AI talent but also XBOX impairment. These are total increases with mixed drivers; no AI amount is given.

The FY2025 MD&A says segment operating expenses rose 1.1bn, 1.5bn and 3.8bn, and R&D rose 3.0bn, 'driven by investments in cloud and AI engineering' (some also by Gaming and Activision). These are total increases with mixed drivers, not AI amounts.

FY2026 MD&A: 'The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins.' The statement gives no amount.

Q3 FY2026 release: AI business 'surpassed an annual revenue run rate of $37 billion, up 123%'. This is a run rate at April 2026, not FY2026 recognized revenue, and the Q4 release gave none. Intelligent Cloud (137,791m) is not the AI line and is excluded.
Q2 FY2025 release: AI business 'surpassed an annual revenue run rate of $13 billion, up 175%'. This is a mid-year run rate, not FY2025 recognized revenue, so it likely understates the full year.
